insights.insight: Ad tech charges $5–$150 CPA for probabilistic attribution; this protocol settles verified purchase signals at ~$0.10 per receipt — a 50–200x cost delta that isn't incremental improvement, it's a different category of signal entirely.

With Chrome cookie deprecation joining Safari and Firefox, device fingerprinting under regulatory pressure, and data brokers facing shrinking legal surface area, the verified receipt is one of the few remaining cookieless signals that doesn't require inference.

Amazon knows Amazon buyers; Walmart knows Walmart buyers; neither knows what the other knows — this protocol's aggregate spans grocery, dining, gas, retail, and DTC simultaneously, making it structurally visible where every first-party silo is structurally blind.

20 distinct non-metro state signals confirmed, spanning both coasts, Southeast interior, upper Midwest, and interior Southwest — with no paid acquisition detected across any observed cycle, indicating word-of-mouth or social graph propagation rather than manufactured growth.

At 3.174–3.176 bits of category entropy, the 14-day receipt window spans restaurants, grocery, department stores, gas/convenience, and digital commerce simultaneously — Walmart, Costco, Amazon, and Shopify all appearing in the same verified dataset is a brand-mix signal most panels can't replicate.

125 receipts in the 14-day window carry an average ticket of ~$290 and a 10.8% store-resolution failure rate, suggesting large-basket or digital commerce transactions that standard retail data sources routinely misclassify or miss entirely.
